angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 242,104 km at 81.85 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.2174 +/- 0.0401 mas (same row, RUWE 1.31): 81.85 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.348 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract): 242,104 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.33 +/- 0.009 solar masses from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3623 +/- 138 K from Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Christiansen et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..244C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-384.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.873, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
